en.headline: HKMU reports information security incident affecting possible data of about 5000 people
en.dek: The university said it identified suspected unauthorised access on 4 November and notified staff and students the next day, while a report said data including HKID numbers was offered for sale.
body: Hong Kong Metropolitan University confirmed it discovered an information security incident involving suspected unauthorised access to its IT systems on 4 November. The university said it immediately activated its emergency response, disabled relevant system functions for investigation, and engaged an independent consultant to assess impact and risks.

In a statement, the university said the extent of the impact and whether any personal data had been disclosed without authorisation remained under investigation. It reported the incident to police and notified the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data, while proactively contacting potentially affected individuals and advising password resets and vigilance against phishing.

A report published early on 16 November said information allegedly offered for sale on the dark web included names of students, Hong Kong identity card numbers, telephone numbers, addresses and grade point averages, potentially affecting about 5,000 people linked to the university. The university has not confirmed the specific number or data fields in its public statement.
Correction: The Chinese dek previously used an incorrect character for 'the next day'; it has been fixed to 翌日.

zh.headline: 都會大學披露資訊安全事件 可能影響約5000人資料
zh.dek: 大學表示11月4日發現疑似未經授權存取，翌日通知員工及學生，報道指包括身份證號碼等資料在暗網出售。
body: 香港都會大學確認於11月4日發現涉及疑似未經授權存取其資訊系統的資訊安全事件。大學表示已即時啟動緊急應變機制，暫停相關系統功能以便調查，並聘請獨立第三方顧問評估影響及風險。
大學在聲明中指出，事件影響範圍及是否有個人資料未經授權披露仍在調查中。校方已向警方報案，並通知個人資料私隱專員公署，同時主動通知可能受影響人士，建議重設密碼及提防釣魚攻擊。
16日凌晨的報道指，暗網出售的資料據稱包括學生姓名、香港身份證號碼、電話、地址及成績平均積點，可能涉及約5000名與大學有關人士。大學的公開聲明未有確認具體人數或資料類別。
更正：中文 dek 先前使用了錯誤字元，已修正為「翌日」。
